headline: ICoAS fraternity reaffirms commitment to cost optimisation for Atmanirbhar Bharat on ICoAS day 2026
fullText:
Ministry of Finance

ICoAS fraternity reaffirms commitment to cost optimisation for Atmanirbhar Bharat on ICoAS day 2026

Secretary Expenditure Shri V. Vualnam expressed his commendation for valuable tireless efforts of ICoAS officers in cost management of Government of India

Defence Secretary Shri. Rajesh Kumar Singh: Financial prudence and commercial expertise assume critical importance during unprecedented transformation of defence sector currently

Secretary Defence Production Shri. Sanjeev Kumar: ICoAS officers support in cost management goes beyond reducing expenditure, and enables better investment decisions

09 AUG 2026 7:34PM by PIB Delhi

Shri. Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary, Department of Defence, Ministry of Defence, graced the Foundation Day celebration of the Indian Cost Accounts Service (ICoAS), organised under the aegis of the Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, as the Chief Guest, in New Delhi today. Shri. Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary, Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, was present on the occasion as the Guest of Honour. This year's celebration was observed under the theme "Role of ICoAS Officers in Cost Optimization for Atmanirbhar Bharat", reflecting the growing significance of cost and fiscal efficiency in furthering India's pursuit of self-reliance leading to Viksit Bharat.

Delivering the keynote address, Shri. Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary, Department of Defence lauded the professionalism, analytical acumen and steadfast dedication of ICoAS officers in strengthening cost management practices across Government Ministries and Departments. He observed that the Service has consistently played a catalytic role in advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat through judicious cost optimization, prudent resource utilisation and robust financial oversight, particularly in Defence Sector.

In his address as Guest of Honour, Shri. Sanjeev Kumar, Secretary, Department of Defence Production, drew attention to the increasing relevance of cost accounting expertise in bolstering indigenous manufacturing capabilities thereby not only reducing India's reliance on imports, but also be competitive in export market. He commended the unique and strategic role of ICoAS officers with the Defence Production ecosystem and called for reinvention of the service and its functioning in the changing defence acquisition scenarios and to develop deeper synergy between ICoAS officers and strategic sectors in furtherance of national self-reliance.

Shri V. Vualnam, Secretary, Department of Expenditure (DoE), Ministry of Finance, conveyed his warm greetings to the officers on the occasion of ICoAS Day 2026 through a video message. He highlighted the valuable contribution of ICoAS officers towards effective cost management in the Government of India. He further emphasized that, with the increasing participation of the private sector and the growing adoption of Public-Private Partnerships (PPPs) in advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat, ICoAS officers will have a significant role in ensuring cost efficiency, appropriate risk allocation and sound project structuring.

On the occasion, a commemorative e-brochure of the ICoAS was released, chronicling the evolution, key functions, notable achievements and capacity-building initiatives undertaken by the Service.

Earlier in the programme, Shri Anand Kumar Pal, Chief Adviser (Cost) and Head of ICoAS conveyed his warm wishes to the officers of ICoAS service and urged them to embrace technology and innovation to be the financial analysts for the Government of India. He also stressed the officers to uphold the highest standards of integrity and professionalism and to adopt latest financial modelling tools; advanced techniques for data visualisation; analytical frameworks that support farsighted financial advice and sound policy design for moving towards Viksit Bharat.

Shri. Rohin Koppuravuri, Joint Director (Cost) gave a presentation on the Service's journey, evolution, its contribution and the future course of action to be undertaken to meet the evolving demands of public financial management and to ensure “Maximum Value for every Rupee spent”.

In recognition of outstanding contribution, six young ICoAS officers were felicitated by Shri. Rajesh Kumar Singh, Secretary, Department of Defence, with 'Sarvottam', 'Ati Uttam’,'Uttam' and 'Protsahan' appreciation certificates instituted to encourage and acknowledge the meritorious efforts of young officers of the Service.

The inaugural session was followed by two engaging technical sessions marking the ICoAS commitment to innovation, continuous learning and professional excellence.

In the first technical session, Shri Nandkumaram spoke on the "Use of Artificial Intelligence in Public Financial Management", elaborating on the transformative potential of Artificial Intelligence in enhancing efficiency and AI Interventions across Public Finance Value Chain for cost and financial management functions across Government.

The second technical session saw Shri Arvind Raj address the officers on "Stress Management", sharing valuable insights and practical strategies to help officers maintain mental well-being and professional resilience amidst demanding official responsibilities.

The celebration drew enthusiastic participation from senior officials across Ministries and Departments, reaffirming the indispensable role of ICoAS in policy formulation, cost management and efficient public expenditure.

ICoAS Day 2026 thus served as a valuable platform for capacity building, knowledge exchange and strategic dialogue, reinforcing the Service's unwavering commitment to a self-reliant and economically resilient Viksit Bharat.

(Release ID: 2296879)

### OVERVIEW  
The Indian Cost Accounts Service (ICoAS) celebrated its Foundation Day 2026 under the theme "Role of ICoAS Officers in Cost Optimization for Atmanirbhar Bharat," highlighting its role in advancing cost management and fiscal efficiency across government sectors, particularly the defence sector, to support India's self-reliance goals.  

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS  
- **Keynote Speakers**: Shri. Rajesh Kumar Singh (Secretary, Department of Defence) and Shri. Sanjeev Kumar (Secretary, Department of Defence Production) emphasized ICoAS officers’ contributions to cost optimization and indigenous manufacturing.

headline: Runway Excursion Incident Involving Cessna C172 trainer Aircraft at Baramati Airfield, Maharashtra
fullText:
Ministry of Civil Aviation

Runway Excursion Incident Involving Cessna C172 trainer Aircraft at Baramati Airfield, Maharashtra

09 AUG 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi

A runway excursion incident involving a Cessna C172 type aircraft, registration VT-SEX, operated by Academy of Carver Aviation, a DGCA approved Flying Training Organization occurred at Baramati Airfield, Maharashtra, on 09 August 2026 at approximately 12:25 PM.

The aircraft was being operated for a Circuit and Landing Emergencies (CL Emergencies) training exercise. The aircraft was under the command of Capt. Chirag Shashikant Doifode, Flight Instructor with trainee Abhijeet Jundre on board.

The aircraft taxied out at approximately 0639 UTC (1209 IST) for the scheduled training exercise. During the exercise, the aircraft entered the runway through Link Bravo and lined up at the threshold of Runway 29, where a rejected take-off exercise practice was carried out. Subsequently, the aircraft lined up at the threshold of Runway 11 and another rejected take-off exercise was carried out.

During the course of the exercise, the aircraft was unable to stop within the paved runway surface and subsequently veered off the extended paved surface beyond the threshold of Runway 29 towards the right side, resulting in a runway excursion.

There were no injuries or fatalities reported. The aircraft has sustained prima facie damage to the propeller, engine cowling and nose landing gear. A detailed assessment of the damage will be carried out by the competent authorities.

The DGCA Air Safety team is proceeding to the site to conduct a preliminary investigation and ascertain the circumstances and contributing factors leading to the incident. Further information will be shared as and when it is verified and becomes available.

(Release ID: 2296861)

A runway excursion involving a Cessna C172 trainer occurred at Baramati Airfield, Maharashtra, on 9 August 2026; no injuries were reported and the aircraft sustained damage to its propeller, engine cowling, and nose landing gear while DGCA investigators began a preliminary inquiry.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS

- Investigation: DGCA Air Safety team on site conducting a preliminary investigation; further findings to be released as verified.

headline: ‘The message of Nasha Mukti from Kashi must reach every village in Jalgaon’ — MoS Raksha Khadse
fullText:
Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

‘The message of Nasha Mukti from Kashi must reach every village in Jalgaon’ — MoS Raksha Khadse

Appeal to turn the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva – Viksit Bharat’ campaign into a people’s movement; Emphasis on collective action by spiritual institutions, saints, administration and youth

09 AUG 2026 6:25PM by PIB Delhi

A special meeting of representatives from spiritual institutions, saints and seers, public representatives, administration, voluntary organizations and social bodies was held today at the District Planning Bhavan, Collector Office, Jalgaon, to give a widespread people’s movement character to the nationwide ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva – Viksit Bharat’ campaign launched on the appeal of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.

Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports, Smt. Raksha Khadse, addressed and guided the meeting through video conferencing.

Also present were Minister Shri Sanjay Savkare, MLA Shri Raju Bhole, District Collector Shri Rohan Ghuge, Superintendent of Police Shri Shrikant Dhivare, CEO Zilla Parishad Smt. Karishma Nair, District Youth Officer, MY Bharat Shri Abhishek Chavare, along with other administrative officials.

Mahamandaleshwar Swami Janardan Hari Ji Maharaj graced the meeting with his presence. Representatives of various spiritual and religious institutions, saints, voluntary organizations and social sector also participated.

“The message of Nasha Mukti from Kashi must reach every village in Jalgaon”

Guiding the meeting, Union Minister of State for Youth Affairs & Sports Smt. Raksha Khadse urged for mass public participation in the Nasha Mukti campaign in Jalgaon district.

She said, The message of Nasha Mukti from Kashi must reach every village in Jalgaon. The energy of our youth should be used not in addiction, but in nation-building. Our effort will be to take the resolve that started from Jalgaon to every family and every young person and transform it into a widespread mass movement. A healthy, empowered and addiction-free youth generation is the real strength of a Viksit Bharat. For building a Nasha Mukt society, it is essential that along with the government, saints, spiritual institutions, social organizations, educational institutions and youth come forward together.”

Decisive role of spiritual institutions and saints

The meeting highlighted that given the wide reach of spiritual institutions and saints across all sections of society in Jalgaon district, their role in taking the message of Nasha Mukti to every village is extremely important. It was emphasized that they should continuously run awareness programs to convey the importance of an addiction-free lifestyle, self-discipline, positive thinking and healthy living to the youth.

Mahamandaleshwar Swami Janardan Hari Ji Maharaj said that the role of family, society and spiritual institutions is crucial in character building of youth.

“To keep youth away from addiction, it is necessary to build their confidence, values and positive outlook towards life. Spiritual institutions and saints will actively participate in this awareness work,” he stated.

Focus on channelizing youth energy in positive directions

It was stated that mere awareness is not enough in de-addiction efforts. Youth must be connected with positive opportunities in sports, education, skill development, employment, volunteering and nation-building. The need for MY Bharat, NSS, youth clubs, educational institutions and social organizations to work in coordination to channelize youth energy into constructive and positive work was expressed.

Active participation of public representatives

Speaking on the occasion, Minister Shri Sanjay Savkare stressed the need for all sections of society to actively participate with the government in the Nasha Mukti campaign.

“Youth are the future of the country. Along with awareness, it is necessary to connect them with positive and constructive initiatives to keep them away from addiction. If this campaign gets public participation, its impact will certainly be widespread,” he said.

MLA Shri Raju Bhole emphasized the need to run continuous local initiatives to take the message of Nasha Mukti to the youth of Jalgaon city as well as the district.

“For a Nasha Mukt society, every family and every citizen must participate in this effort. Giving youth the right direction and positive opportunities is our collective responsibility,” he said.

Action through coordination of administration and social organizations

The meeting discussed implementing continuous activities through coordination of MY Bharat, NSS, youth clubs, educational institutions, voluntary organizations, sports bodies, spiritual institutions and local administration for effective execution of the campaign.

An appeal was made for various organizations to actively participate through their platforms to take the message of Nasha Mukti to every village in Jalgaon district, create awareness among youth and build a positive environment to stay away from addiction.

Under the leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, it was resolved to give the ‘Nasha Mukt Yuva – Viksit Bharat’ campaign the form of a widespread people’s movement in Jalgaon district and take the message of Nasha Mukti to every village, every family and every youth.

(Release ID: 2296858)

headline: Text of PM’s interaction with India's CWG champions
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Text of PM’s interaction with India's CWG champions

10 AUG 2026 1:11PM by PIB Delhi

प्रधानमंत्री – मेरे यहां, मुझे यहां लगभग 12-13 साल हो गए इसी मकान में, अगर मैंने regularly और हर बार किसी को रिसिव किया है, किसी को मैं मिला हूं, तो खिलाड़ी हैं। पिछले 10-12 साल हो गए, आप लोगों के पुरुषार्थ के कारण, भारत को लगातार विजय दिलाने के आपके प्रयासों के कारण और उत्तरोत्तर सफलता में नई ऊंचाईयां पार करने की परंपरा के कारण, जो काम शायद हम स्कूलों में जाकर कहें कि नहीं नहीं भई खेलना चाहिए, ये करना चाहिए, वो काम स्कूलों में जाकर के हम कर सकते थे, उससे ज्यादा आपका मेडल उनको inspire करता है।

प्रधानमंत्री – तुमने मुझे वादा किया था पिछली बार कि तुम्हारी दोनों बेटियां खिलाड़ी बन जाएंगी?

खिलाड़ी - हाँ जी अभी वे उमर की छोटी हैं, अगले कॉमनवेल्थ में एक घर में तीन मेडल लाकर दिखाएंगी।

प्रधानमंत्री – पक्का।

खिलाड़ी – हाँ जी।

खिलाड़ी – जब मैं दौड़ रहा था, जब मेरा इवेंट था 29 को, तो उस दिन गुरुपूर्णिमा थी, तो उस दिन मेरे गुरू को मैंने एक गिफ्ट दे दिया।

प्रधानमंत्री – बड़ी शान बढ़ाई आपने। इतनी आंसू टपक रहे थे, मुझे लगता है कि आंसू के हर बूंद से जैसे गोल्ड मेडल टपक रहा है।

खिलाड़ी – मैं बहुत ज्यादा खुशी थी, इमोशनल भी थे उसी दिन, खुशी ज्यादा था और मैं इसलिए रोई थी कि मेरा पेरिस आलंपिक में मेरा 1 Kg में मेडल रह गई थी और एक प्लेयर्स की लाइफ में क्या क्या हमको फेस करना पड़ता है। तो ये 4 साल के अंदर में कितना क्या क्या कुछ मैंने फेस किया था, हर टाइम injury ही चल रहे थे और family problem, वो सब हो रहा था। तो बहुत मुश्किल से मैं ये 4 साल फेस किया था। तो वो सब जब पोडियम में जब मैं खड़ी थी सर और हमारी जो फ्लैग ऊपर जाते हैं और हमारे नेशनल एंथम जब बजते हैं तो सर हम रुक नहीं सकते सर, अपना आप आंसू निकलते हैं।

प्रधानमंत्री – बहुत बहुत बढ़िया

प्रधानमंत्री – आपके इस अचीवमेंट को सिर्फ आपका अचीवमेंट मानता हूं, ऐसा नहीं है, ये आपका विजय आने वाली पीढ़ियों के लिए बहुत बड़ी प्रेरणा बन जाता है।

खिलाड़ी – सब डर रहे थे हमसे कि इंडिया के साथ फाइट आ गई, अब तो हम पहली फाइट ही हार जायेंगे, हमारा मेडल भी नहीं आयेगा।

प्रधानमंत्री – यानी मान के चलते हैं।

खिलाड़ी – हाँ सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – क्या हुआ, वो restaurant वालों से झगड़ा कर रही थी?

खिलाड़ी – हम लोगों का जो इतना अच्छा परफॉर्मेंस था, लास्ट डे था और सब जीत के गए थे और पूरा इंडिया के लोग थे। तो थोड़ा सा मुझे बुरा लग रहा। तो मैंने उनको अच्छे से बोला रिक्वेस्ट किया था सर, फिर उन्होंने मान भी लिया, अभी चेंज भी हो गया सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – इस विजय की परिस्थिति खुशी, आनंद, अपने साथियों के साथ और गेम पूरे हो चुके हैं। तो हसी मजाक मस्ती का मूड ऐसे समय उस मैप पर नजर जाना और उसको रजिस्टर करना और तुरंत सिर्फ मेडल लेते समय देश खड़ा हो जाता है ऐसा नहीं, भीतर से देश का भाव मैं सच बताता हूँ ये वीडियो सामान्य नहीं है आपका, लंबे समय तक लोगों को याद रहेगा। ये बॉक्सिंग वालों से भी दुनिया के खिलाड़ी अब डरने लगे हैं।

खिलाड़ी – जरूर सर, पुरे सभी डरे हुए थे। एक के बाद एक गोल्ड मेडल गोल्ड मेडल आ रहे थे और मतलब पूरा लास्ट में ऐसे धमाका जैसा हो गया बिल्कुल। जिस तरीके से हम लोगों को सपोर्ट मिल रहा है, हमें बैक टू बैक कंपटीशन मिल रहा है वो एक बहुत बड़ी बात है और हमारे जितने भी यंग एथलीट है वो लोग सभी जैसे खेलो इंडिया स्कीम से आए हुए हैं और ये एक बहुत बड़ा changes ला रहा है पूरे स्पोर्ट्स में ही।

प्रधानमंत्री – अगर आप लोग खेलो इंडिया की प्रतिष्ठा बढ़ाते हैं और प्रतिष्ठा सिर्फ वहां जाकर के रिबिन काटने से नहीं होगी। आप वैसे ही खेलेंगे जैसे एक छोटा विद्यार्थी, एक छोटा नौजवान, छोटा खिलाड़ी खेलता है। यह बहुत बड़ा कंट्रीब्यूशन करेगा। क्योंकि अभी तो हमें बहुत आगे जाना है, बहुत मेडल लाना है। कारगिल विजय दिवस पर किसकी विजय हुई थी?

खिलाड़ी – उस दिन कारगिल डे था वैसे और जिस दिन मैंने पाकिस्तान के साथ फाइट किया था सर, वो उसी दिन का था। तो मैं एक इंडियन आर्मी से हूं, तो मैंने उस दिन मैं पहले से बहुत वो था कि सर पाकिस्तान को हराना है। तो मैंने वो पाकिस्तान एक तरफ मैंने 5-0 से हराया, तो मैंने हमारा इंडियन आर्मी का कारगिल हीरोज़ को मैंने डेडिकेट किया किया था सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – आपको यह याद रहना और आप स्वयं फौज से हैं तो, मैं जरूर मानता हूं कि देश के वीर जवानों को आपने जो भाव प्रकट किया ना कि, मैं कारगिल के विजेताओं को मेरा मेडल समर्पित करता हूं। उसने उस विजय पर चार चांद लगा दिए और जिसको पराजित करना था उसी को किया आपने।

खिलाड़ी – वो पाकिस्तान की बात चल रही है, मुझे किस्सा याद आ गया सर। 2015 वर्ल्ड मिलिट्री गेम थे और मेरी पाकिस्तान के साथ पहली फाइट आ गई थी और वर्ल्ड मिलिट्री गेम थे तो मिलिट्री वाले के फोन आए कि भई पाकिस्तान से नहीं हारना है। तो फिर मैं फर्स्ट राउंड 4-1 से जीत गया। सेकंड राउंड 3-2 से जीत गया, पर दोनों के सर लग गए आपस में, तो दोनों के लग गए कट और फाइट तो मैं जीत गया।

प्रधानमंत्री – हाँ

खिलाड़ी – उसके बाद फिर दोनों चले गए हॉस्पिटल में टांके लगवाने के लिए। फिर 2014 में आप फर्स्ट टाइम प्रधानमंत्री जी बने थे और जो हमारे साथ आर्मी का कोच गया हुआ था उसका नाम नरेंद्र राणा था और फिर वो कई देर तक सोच के मेरे को बोला कि भाईजान एक बात बोलूं, मैं हां बोलो, बोला भाईजान आपका नाम नरेंद्र है। आपके कोच का नाम नरेंद्र है, आपके प्रधानमंत्री का नाम नरेंद्र है, तो मुझे नरेंद्र नाम से नफरत हो गई है।

प्रधानमंत्री – सिर्फ आपने मेडल की संख्या बढ़ाई ऐसा नहीं है। आपने एक पीढ़ी को तैयार किया।

खिलाड़ी – मेरे मन में भी धक-धक धक-धक हो रहा है सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – आप चिंता मत कीजिए।

प्रधानमंत्री – आप चाहें तो आपको बोलने में भी मेडल मिलने वाला है।

खिलाड़ी – मेरे फ्रेंड सर्कल में किसी ने बोला था कि मैं उनको कुछ बोलती थी भई तुम्हारे अच्छे के लिए तुम करो। तो अक्सर मुझे वो बोलते थे कि तू के मोदी ते मिल रही है?

खिलाड़ी – हरियाणवी में बोल देते हैं सर कि क्या तू मोदी से मिली हुई है, कि तेरी बात माने। तो आज मैं आपसे मिली हूं सर। मैं उनको बोल पाऊंगी कि हां मैं मोदी जी से मिली हूं।

खिलाड़ी – कॉमनवेंल्थ गेम्स में मैंने सिल्वर मेडल जीता, फिर मैंने क्रेडिट साहब को दिया, सपना तो था एक बार मेडल जीत के लेके आने के लिए, बट ट्रेनिंग का सेंटर नहीं था, मैंने SAI आने के बाद मैं बहुत ट्रेनिंग करके मेडल जीत पा रहा, इसलिए बहुत खुशी से मैंने सर को क्रेडिट दिया था क्योंकि बहुत इंप्रूव हुआ।

प्रधानमंत्री – मेरे लिए बहुत बड़ा सम्मान का विषय है, मेहनत आपने की और मुझे याद किया, मैं आपका बहुत आभारी हूं दोस्त।

प्रधानमंत्री – वाराणसी में खेल तुम प्रैक्टिस कर रही थी ना?

खिलाड़ी – जी सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – कैसा बना है स्टेडियम?

खिलाड़ी – सर अच्छा बना है, वहां पर मैं 10-12 दिन के लिए ट्रेनिंग करने गई थी, क्योंकि मैं मंदिर गई थी तो वहां पर ही ट्रेनिंग करके आई थी। और मैं वहां पे मतलब सेटल भी होना चाहती हूं क्योंकि मुझे काशी विश्वनाथ बहुत अच्छा लगता है सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – भोपाल में ट्रेनिंग कर रही थी ना?

प्रधानमंत्री – तो उज्जैन जाते थे कि नहीं?

खिलाड़ी – जी सर उज्जैन भी गई थी सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – अच्छा महाकाल के पास भी गई।

प्रधानमंत्री – काशी विश्वनाथ के पास हो आई एक बार।

प्रधानमंत्री – सावन महीना तो अभी है।

खिलाड़ी – वहां घर जाके फिर उसके बाद जाऊंगी सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – ठीक है।

खिलाड़ी – साई ने भी सर बहुत सपोर्ट किया है मुझे। इसके कारण ही मैं यहां तक पहुंची हूं सर। और मैं खेलो इंडिया स्कीम में भी थी 2018 में जो फर्स्ट खेलो इंडिया हुआ था, उसमें मेरा सिल्वर मेडल था, वहां पे भी मैंने आपको देखा था ओपनिंग सेरेमनी में, तो उसमें मेरा मेडल था, तो मेरे को स्कीम भी मिल गया और मैं यहां तक पहुंची हूं सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – स्पोर्ट्स व्यवस्था एक बात है, लेकिन देश मेडल तब प्राप्त करता है जब देश में स्पोर्ट्स कल्चर बनता है। दोस्तों आपने बहुत बड़ा काम किया है। देश का नाम रोशन किया है। आपको मैं बहुत बधाई देता हूं और आप विश्वास कीजिए आगे भी आप विजयी होंगे और फिर से एक बार यहीं पर हम मिलेंगे। बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद। बहुत-बहुत शुभकामनाएं।

प्रधानमंत्री – ये लगातार तीसरी बार देश को मेडल दिलवाया है।

खिलाड़ी – थैंक यू सर।

प्रधानमंत्री – बहुत आशीर्वाद बेटा।

खिलाड़ी – और थैंक यू सो मच मैं सर के हाथ से लड्डू खा रही मेरा कल बर्थडे था तो आज सर के हाथ से…

प्रधानमंत्री – बहुत बधाई वाह।

प्रधानमंत्री – मुस्कुराओ यार ।

प्रधानमंत्री – जो खेलेगा वो खिलेगा।

headline: Asiatic Lion population rises from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025; Reflects dedication of Forest Officials, Conservationists and Local Communities: Shri Bhupender Yadav
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

Asiatic Lion population rises from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025; Reflects dedication of Forest Officials, Conservationists and Local Communities: Shri Bhupender Yadav

On World Lion Day, Union Environment Minister reaffirms India’s commitment to Wildlife and Biodiversity Conservation

10 AUG 2026 12:02PM by PIB Delhi

On World Lion Day 2026, Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, celebrated India’s remarkable journey in lion conservation and reaffirmed the country’s unwavering commitment to protecting wildlife and biodiversity.

In a post on social media, the Minister noted that the Asiatic Lion population has steadily increased from 523 in 2015 to 891 in 2025. He attributed this achievement to the dedication of forest officials, conservationists, local communities and all those working tirelessly to protect the magnificent species.

🦁 On World Lion Day, we celebrate India’s remarkable journey in lion conservation.

India’s success in conserving the Asiatic Lion is a proud testament to our unwavering commitment to wildlife and biodiversity. From protecting critical habitats to strengthening conservation… pic.twitter.com/7aJv98uRSG

— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) August 10, 2026

Shri Yadav stated that India’s success in conserving the Asiatic Lion is a proud testament to the country’s commitment to wildlife and biodiversity. He reaffirmed the resolve to safeguard India’s natural heritage and ensure that the roar of the Asiatic Lion continues to resonate for generations to come.

On the occasion, in a social media post, Union MoS (EFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, stated that by protecting critical habitats, strengthening conservation programmes and fostering coexistence, India has shown the world that development and nature can thrive together.

On #WorldLionDay, we honour India’s extraordinary journey in conserving the majestic Asiatic Lion.

From 523 lions in 2015 to 891 in 2025, this remarkable growth reflects the tireless efforts of forest officers, frontline workers, conservationists, local communities & countless… pic.twitter.com/FCkRYqPwEI

— Kirti Vardhan Singh (@KVSinghMPGonda) August 10, 2026

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi announced 'Project Lion' on 15th August, 2020, to ensure long term conservation of the big cat. Currently, the lion range has expanded from around 30,000 sq. km. in 2020 to nearly 35,000 sq. km.

The project adopts a landscape-level, holistic approach to biodiversity conservation, emphasising habitat enhancement, disease monitoring and veterinary support, scientific population tracking, technology-aided interventions, biodiversity protection, benefit sharing and community involvement.

headline: PAIMANA: Strengthening Data-Driven Infrastructure Governance
fullText:
PIB Backgrounder

PAIMANA: Strengthening Data-Driven Infrastructure Governance

10 AUG 2026 11:47AM by PIB Delhi

PAIMANA – An Overview

Efficient monitoring of infrastructure projects is essential for timely implementation, transparency and governance. To support this, PAIMANA (Project Assessment, Infrastructure Monitoring and Analytics for Nation-Building) was launched on 25 September 2025 as a web-based platform for monitoring Central Sector infrastructure projects in India. The platform replaces the earlier OCMS-2006 (Online Computerized Monitoring System). Developed by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), PAIMANA is used for monitoring ongoing Central Sector infrastructure projects costing ₹150 crore or more.

MoSPI has launched a module called PAIMANA-CRIP on 08th July 2026, replacing DPIIT’s Integrated Project Monitoring Portal (IPMP), envisioned to evolve as Central Repository of Infrastructure Projects. The project-related data for PRAGATI (Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation), PMG and other review mechanisms would subsequently be sourced and updated through the same.

Over 20+ Ministries/Departments/ Implementing Agencies regularly update the information of projects on PAIMANA-CRIP through data entry or via API (Application Programming Interfaces) modes.

Currently, the Project Monitoring vertical of the PAIMANA portal is integrated with DPIIT’s IPMP/ IIG through API-based data exchange. Over 60 per cent of projects on PAIMANA are being updated automatically through APIs from the MIS or web platforms of respective Ministries/ Departments.

In addition to strengthening project monitoring, PAIMANA has expanded its role to support infrastructure performance monitoring through a dedicated Performance Monitoring Dashboard. Launched on 16th April, 2026, the dashboard tracks infrastructure performance across major sub-sectors through a comprehensive set of indicators. It marks a significant advancement towards data-driven governance and evidence-based policymaking.

Performance Monitoring Dashboard at a Glance

The Performance Monitoring Dashboard brings together performance indicators across key infrastructure sectors in a unified digital platform. The indicators are compiled from official data provided/published by the concerned Ministries and Departments and are updated periodically based on the latest available information. The dashboard presents these data through interactive visualizations and analytical tools, enabling users to monitor trends and assess sectoral performance over time.

Key Features of the Performance Monitoring Dashboard

The Performance Monitoring Dashboard is built on a comprehensive indicator framework developed in consultation with the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP). The framework aligns with the Harmonized Master List (HML) of Infrastructure (2022), issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), which serves as the national classification framework for infrastructure sectors eligible for policy support, investment planning and financing-related benefits.

Indicators have been streamlined to prevent overlap with established indices. Examples include the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) and the Eight Core Industries.

A detailed indicator framework spans six infrastructure sub-sectors. These are Power, Civil Aviation, Telecommunications, Railways, Roads, and Ports, Shipping & Waterways.

The Performance Monitoring Dashboard has now been expanded to 165 indicators. This expansion includes the addition of 54 new indicators, significantly enhancing the comprehensiveness of infrastructure performance monitoring.

A single digital interface allows monitoring of performance sector by sector. It offers interactive visualisation and time-series analysis for policymakers, researchers and stakeholders.

A centralised dashboard delivers one cross-sector view of infrastructure sectors. This capability deepens inter-sectoral analysis.

The current framework gauges sectoral performance through growth rates. It reviews year-on-year, month-on-month and cumulative growth, targets and capacity utilisation in chosen sectors.

Distribution of Performance Indicators Across Sub-sectors (as on 16th July, 2026)

S. No | Infrastructure Sub-sector | Total Number of Indicators

1 | Civil Aviation | 31

4 | Ports, Shipping & Waterways | 62

5 | Telecommunications | 13

6 | Railways | 37

The Revamped Monitoring Approach

The revamped approach marks a shift from measuring sectoral outputs (production) to assessing multi-dimensional infrastructure performance across the dimensions of access: which measure how widely infrastructure is available; quality: which assess its usefulness and reliability; fiscal cost & revenue: which assess allocation and use of financial resources for infrastructure; utilization: evaluate how efficiently infrastructure is used for its defined purpose; affordability: determine whether it is economically accessible to people. The above categorisation of indicators improves analysis by moving beyond simple output tracking to a more holistic evaluation of infrastructure performance across multiple dimensions, enabling informed policy decisions and targeted interventions.

Engaging Stakeholders

Stakeholders, including concerned Ministries and Departments, receive regular updates on their project execution. These updates draw on the data analytics generated within PAIMANA. Such analytics help them act wherever project execution needs attention.

Ongoing coordination takes place through monthly review meetings and other exchanges. This practice reinforces evidence-based monitoring by providing timely updates on performance indicators.

Login credentials for tailored dashboards are available with every Line Ministry and Department. Consequently, they can directly access the portal to review project progress.

Infrastructure Projects Monitored (Data as of June 2026)

As of June 2026, 1,847 ongoing projects were under watch across 17 Central Ministries and Departments. Together they carry a revised cost of ₹ 40.54 lakh crore.

Spending on these projects has so far reached ₹ 21.97 lakh crore. This equals about 54.18 per cent of the revised cost, reflecting steady advancement.

Many projects have reached advanced stages of completion. Around 709 projects (~39%) exceed 80% physical progress. About 337 projects (~19%) have passed 80% financial completion.

The Transport & Logistics sector leads in the number of ongoing projects. It holds 1,341 projects worth ₹22.32 lakh crore, reflecting the focus on connectivity.

The ongoing infrastructure projects include 769 mega projects, each costing ₹1,000 crore or more, worth ₹30.51 lakh crore.

They also include 1,078 major projects, each costing ₹150–1,000 crore, worth ₹5.10 lakh crore.

Ministry / Department-wise Progress of Infrastructure Projects

The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways records the largest project count. It manages 1,022 projects (55%) with a revised cost share of Rs. 9.89 lakh crore (24%).

headline: ACHIEVEMENTS AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT UNDER THE PM SVANIDHI SCHEME
fullText:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs

ACHIEVEMENTS AND SOCIO-ECONOMIC IMPACT UNDER THE PM SVANIDHI SCHEME

10 AUG 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) Scheme was launched on 1st June, 2020 with the objective of facilitating collateral free working capital term loans to urban street vendors. Since scheme inception till 12th July 2026, 76.95 lakh street vendors have availed more than 1.15 crore collateral-free loans amounting to ₹18,475 crore.

The scheme has achieved significant milestones in providing institutional credit to urban street vendors and promoting their financial inclusion. The impact of the Scheme has been assessed through studies conducted by the Indian School of Business (ISB), Hyderabad in 2023 and 2025.

The 2023 study was conducted in 100 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) across the country covering more than 5,000 beneficiaries and it found that PM SVANidhi was the first loan from a bank for 95% of the beneficiaries and the loan was utilized for expanding their business. The 2025 study was conducted in 99 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) across the country covering more than 5,000 beneficiaries (with around 60% of the respondents being part of the 2023 study sample) and it found that the average annualized business income among PM SVANidhi borrowers grew by around 20 percent, between 2023 and 2025.

Around 30 percent of borrowers across all cycles reported holding loans other than PM SVANidhi loans which underscores the scheme’s role in building credit histories for vendors who previously had little or no access to formal credit. Further the study also found that between 2023 and 2025, the adoption of digital payments among street vendors rose significantly.

The study also found the scheme’s impact extends well beyond business recovery. By easing credit constraints and stabilizing household cash flows, the scheme has enabled vendor families to improve living conditions, strengthen food security, enhance access to health-care, and support children’s education.

Under PM SVANidhi Scheme, repayment of loans enables street vendors to graduate to higher loan tranches, reflecting improved financial growth. As on 12th July 2026, 29.71 lakh vendors have availed the 2nd loan tranche, and 8.49 lakh vendors have availed the 3rd loan tranche.

Under PM SVANidhi Scheme, for promoting digital adoption, street vendor beneficiaries are incentivized with a cashback of upto ₹100 per month for a period of 12 months (maximum digital incentive of ₹1200/year), for every tranche of loan provided to the street vendor. Further, the restructured scheme provisions for cashback of maximum ₹100 per quarter for 4 quarters to street vendor beneficiaries for conducting digital transactions on wholesale purchases of at least ₹2,000.

Since inception of the scheme till May 2026, over 875 crore digital transactions have been carried out and an amount of ₹412 crore has been released as cash back incentive to the street vendor beneficiaries under the scheme.

‘SVANidhi se Samriddhi’ component under the PM SVANidhi Scheme, was launched on 04 January, 2021, to build social safety net for the beneficiaries and their family members. This facilitates linkages to eight selected Central Government welfare schemes. These 8 Schemes are (i) Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (ii) PM Suraksha Bima Yojana (iii) Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (iv) Registration under Building and other Constructions Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act (BOCW) (v) Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan Yojana (vi) National Food Security Act (NFSA) portability benefit – One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC) (vii) Pradhan Mantri Janani Suraksha Yojana and (viii) Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY).

As on 12th July 2026, socio economic profiling is completed of 50.63 lakh PM SVANidhi beneficiaries, and a total of 1.56 crore scheme sanctions have been extended to them.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

headline: GIS-BASED URBAN PLANNING & MODERNISATION OF MASTER PLANS
fullText:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs

GIS-BASED URBAN PLANNING & MODERNISATION OF MASTER PLANS

10 AUG 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

As per 12th Schedule of the Constitution of India, urban planning including preparation of master plans for cities are the function of Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/ Urban Development Authorities. Government of India supplements the efforts of the States through schematic interventions/ advisories. The Government of India supplements the efforts of States and Union Territories (UTs) through schematic interventions/ advisories and guidelines.

The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has undertaken several initiatives to promote GIS-based urban planning and preparation of digital Master Plans for cities/ULBs. Under Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)/AMRUT 2.0, a dedicated sub-scheme on GIS-based Master Planning is being implemented with the objective of strengthening urban planning systems through creation of geospatial databases, digital base maps and GIS-enabled Master Plans for statutory planning and infrastructure development. ‘Formulation of GIS based Master Plan for AMRUT Cities’ has been approved as a 100% centrally funded sub-scheme under AMRUT and ‘Formulation of GIS based Master Plans for Class-II towns with the population 50,000 - 99,999 has been launched under AMRUT 2.0.

The Ministry has also issued the Urban and Regional Development Plans Formulation and Implementation (URDPFI) Guidelines, which encourage the adoption of GIS-based planning tools and geospatial technologies for evidence-based urban planning and land management.

So far, under AMRUT, Sub-Scheme on Formulation of GIS-based Master Plans for AMRUT Cities, 461 AMRUT cities across 35 States/UTs have been onboarded, Final Geospatial Databases have been prepared for 437 cities, Draft GIS-based Master Plans have been prepared for 404 cities, out of which 292 Master Plans have been finalized. Further, so far, under AMRUT 2.0, Sub-Scheme on Formulation of GIS-based Master Plans for Class-II towns with the population 50,000 - 99,999, covers 875 towns, Draft Geospatial Databases have been prepared for 399 towns, out of which 100 have been finalized. Draft GIS-based Master Plans have been prepared for 136 towns, of which 93 have been finalized.

GIS-based planning enables integration and analysis of spatial information relating to existing land use, transport networks, water supply, sewerage, drainage, public amenities, environmentally sensitive areas and proposed infrastructure. However, enforcement of Master Plans, building bye-laws and action against unauthorised construction falls within the jurisdiction of the respective State Governments/ULBs and Urban Development Authorities. The impact on unauthorised construction consequently depends upon regular updating of GIS data, integration with online building-permission and enforcement systems, and action by the concerned State/ULBs.

The geo-databases created under the two Sub-Schemes have been integrated with the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan (NMP), and the geo-databases for 343 towns have been uploaded on the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan Portal, thereby enabling coordinated infrastructure planning across sectors.

The Ministry has undertaken several measures to expand GIS-based urban planning across Urban Local Bodies. The GIS-based Master Plan Sub-Schemes are being implemented in 461 Class-I cities and 875 Class-II towns across the country. Standardised geospatial databases are being created using state-of-the-art GIS technologies, with Very High Resolution Satellite (VHRS) imagery at 1:4000 scale under the AMRUT GIS Sub-Scheme in accordance with the MoHUA Design & Standards (May 2016), and both VHRS imagery at 1:4000 scale and Drone/UAV mapping at 1:1000 scale under the AMRUT 2.0 GIS Sub-Scheme in accordance with the MoHUA Design & Standards (October 2020) for the creation of GIS base layers for the preparation of Master Plans. The geospatial databases are being uploaded on the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan Portal to promote data sharing and integrated planning. The Ministry also conducts regular review meetings with States/UTs and implementing agencies to monitor progress and resolve implementation issues. Capacity building is being undertaken through technical workshops, training programmes and handholding support for States/UTs and Urban Local Bodies; under the AMRUT GIS Sub-Scheme, about 2,968 officials have been trained through 79 capacity-building programmes, while under the AMRUT 2.0 GIS Sub-Scheme, about 2,648 officials have been trained through 34 capacity-building programmes. These initiatives are contributing to the development of a GIS-enabled digital planning ecosystem for the preparation, revision and implementation of Master Plans using modern geospatial technologies.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

headline: APEDA Facilitates First-Ever Export of Mustard Honey by Dergang FPO from Tripura to Dubai
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

APEDA Facilitates First-Ever Export of Mustard Honey by Dergang FPO from Tripura to Dubai

1 MT export opens new international market opportunities for Dergang FPO and local beekeepers

10 AUG 2026 6:02PM by PIB Delhi

APEDA facilitated the first-ever export of 1 Metric Tonne of Mustard Honey by Dergang Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO) from Tripura to Dubai. The export marks a new milestone for the FPO and the region by creating an opportunity for local beekeepers and farmers to access international markets through organised export-oriented production.

The shipment represents the first-ever export of Mustard Honey from the area and opens new avenues for diversification of Tripura's honey value chain. The initiative is expected to encourage local farmers and FPOs to explore export opportunities and strengthen their participation in international agricultural markets.

The export is expected to provide farmers associated with Dergang FPO with improved price realisation compared to prevailing local market opportunities. Better market access through exports can provide an additional income avenue for beekeepers while encouraging greater adoption of quality-focused and export-oriented honey production practices.

The initiative was supported and hand-held by M/s Salt Range Foods Pvt. Ltd. which has been working with Dergang FPO to strengthen bee production and facilitate the development of export-oriented honey supply. The collaboration has enabled the FPO to take its first step towards international market access while creating a structured opportunity for farmers to participate in the export value chain.

The milestone is significant for Tripura's emerging agri-export ecosystem, particularly for the development of its honey and beekeeping sector. The state's diverse agricultural landscape and growing focus on organised farmer collectives offer considerable potential for expanding the production and export of quality honey and other agricultural products.

The export of Mustard Honey demonstrates the potential of FPO-led aggregation and industry collaboration in connecting farmers with international markets. It is expected to encourage more FPOs and farmers in Tripura and the wider North Eastern Region to explore value addition, quality improvement and export opportunities.

Encouraging the initiative, Agriculture Minister Shri Ratan Lal Nath, said, “The first-ever export of Mustard Honey by Dergang FPO is a significant achievement for Tripura’s beekeepers and farmers. It demonstrates the potential of our local agricultural products to reach international markets and create better income opportunities for farming communities. The Government of Tripura remains committed to strengthening apiculture and organic agriculture while supporting Farmer Producer Organisations in accessing wider markets. With coordinated efforts by farmers, FPOs, exporters and institutions such as APEDA, Tripura can further expand its presence in the global market for quality agricultural and organic products.”

The export consignment was flagged off by Agriculture Minister, Government of Tripura Shri Ratan Lal Nath. The ceremony was attended by Secretary, Agriculture & Horticulture, Government of Tripura Shri Apurba Roy, IAS, Executive Director, IFOAM Organics Asia Ms Jennifer Chang, senior officers from APEDA, representatives of the exporter, logistics partners and progressive beekeepers from the region.

APEDA continues to work with State Governments, FPOs, exporters, processors and other stakeholders to facilitate agricultural exports from the North Eastern Region through market linkages, capacity building, quality assurance and export facilitation. Such initiatives contribute to creating sustainable market opportunities for farmers while expanding the global footprint of India's diverse agricultural products.

headline: Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala Assumes Charge as Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences
fullText:
Ministry of Earth Sciences

Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala Assumes Charge as Secretary, Ministry of Earth Sciences

10 AUG 2026 5:51PM by PIB Delhi

Eminent oceanographer and distinguished scientist Dr. Srinivasa Kumar Tummala officially assumed charge as the Secretary of the Ministry of Earth Sciences (MoES), Government of India. He takes over from Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, who had been handling the responsibilities of MoES under an additional charge. The position was previously held on a full-time basis by Dr. M. Ravichandran. Dr. Tummala’s appointment marks a pivotal and strategic transition for the Ministry of Earth Sciences as India aggressively scales up its flagship Deep Ocean Mission, enhances climate modeling capabilities, and fortifies its multi-hazard early warning infrastructure to protect coastal communities and advance the national Blue Economy agenda.

STRATEGIC VISION FOR MoES

With over three decades of exceptional experience across remote sensing, satellite oceanography, coastal hazard mitigation, and disaster management, Dr. Tummala brings a wealth of techno-managerial leadership to MoES. His leadership arrives at a vital juncture as India expands its scientific footprint across oceanography, polar research, meteorological disaster prevention, and sustainable marine resource exploitation.

A LEGACY OF LEADERSHIP & GLOBAL SERVICE

Prior to taking over as Secretary, MoES, Dr. Tummala held key national and international leadership positions:

Head, ICG/IOTWMS Secretariat, UNESCO-IOC (Perth, Australia): Directed regional tsunami warning networks across 28 Indian Ocean Member States, leading global standardization of ocean watch operations and championing the implementation of the Tsunami Ready Community Recognition Programme.

Director, ESSO-INCOIS (Hyderabad): Served as Director of the Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services starting August 2020. Under his stewardship, INCOIS significantly advanced its Potential Fishing Zone (PFZ) advisories, Coral Reef Bleaching Alert systems, and multi-hazard vulnerability mapping.

Architect of India's Tsunami Early Warning System: Following the devastating 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami, Dr. Tummala acted as Project Manager to establish the state-of-the-art Indian Tsunami Early Warning System at INCOIS, transforming it into a globally designated Tsunami Service Provider (TSP).

MAJOR NATIONAL RECOGNITION & ACADEMIC CONTRIBUTIONS

National Geoscience Award (2010): Conferred by the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, for path-breaking efforts in establishing India's world-class tsunami early warning facilities.

Indian National Geospatial Award (2008): Awarded by the Indian Society of Remote Sensing (ISRS) for innovative contributions to geospatial technologies in disaster mitigation and marine resource mapping.

Global Academic Footprint: Authored over 100 peer-reviewed scientific publications in reputed international journals and served as Vice-Chair of the UNESCO Intergovernmental Coordination Group.

Under Dr. Tummala's strategic leadership, the Ministry of Earth Sciences will continue to strengthen India's observational networks, atmospheric modeling, deep-ocean exploration technologies, and societal services to bolster climate resilience and ocean health across the region.

headline: Independence Day Celebrations 2026 to honour ‘150 Years of Vande Mataram’ & ‘Yuva Shakti for Viksit Bharat@2047’
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

Independence Day Celebrations 2026 to honour ‘150 Years of Vande Mataram’ & ‘Yuva Shakti for Viksit Bharat@2047’

In a first, ‘Vande Mataram’ to be sung from the ramparts of the historic Red Fort

Prime Minister to unfurl the National Flag & address the Nation

Approx. 5,000 Special Guests invited to witness the grand celebrations

10 AUG 2026 5:48PM by PIB Delhi

The Nation will mark its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026, with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi leading the celebrations from the historic Red Fort in Delhi. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi on August 10, 2026, Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh stated that as 2026 marks 150 years of ‘Vande Mataram’, the National Song that inspired millions during the freedom struggle will be sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort for the first time as a tribute to its enduring legacy.

‘Vande Mataram’ will be sung upon the Prime Minister’s arrival at Red Fort. Thereafter, he will unfurl the National Flag and deliver the customary address to the Nation. The celebrations this year will also commemorate Yuva Shakti, acknowledging the contribution of young India in building a Viksit Bharat by 2047, the Defence Secretary added.

150 years of Vande Mataram

The floral decoration will showcase ‘Vande Mataram’, with a total of 2,500 boy & girl cadets of NCC and My Bharat volunteers forming ‘वंदे मातरम्’ on Gyanpath opposite the Rampart. A Mi-17 helicopter of the Indian Air Force will carry a banner commemorating 150 years of ‘Vande Mataram’, and shower flower petals over the people gathered at Red Fort.

Military Band Performances

Paying tribute to the anthem that united and inspired generations during the freedom struggle, a number of band performances are being held pan-India from August 08, 2026. The performances by the bands of Army, Navy, Air Force, Indian Coast Guard, NCC, Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP), Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB), Border Security Force (BSF), Integrated Defence Staff (IDS), Railway Protection Force (RPF) and Assam Rifles at 343 prominent locations will continue till August 15, 2026. Entry to these band performance venues is open to the public to promote patriotic fervour among citizens.

Yuva Shakti: Leading the journey to Viksit Bharat @2047

The Independence Day Celebrations 2026 will acknowledge the success of youth in different spheres. Achievements of 19 medalist students of International Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Mathematical Olympiad 2026 is an example of the success of Yuva Shakti in the field of science. They have been invited for the function and will be seated on the rampart.

View cutters in the backdrop will showcase India’s progress in nuclear and space technology, with the floral decoration at the Guard of Honour area depicting India’s journey to Viksit Bharat @ 2047.

Approx. 5,000 Special Guests, who are achievers from different walks of life and are guiding the country in its Viksit Bharat journey, have been invited as Special Guests for the celebrations. The categories include:

Youth innovators under National Innovation Programmes

Best interns under Prime Minister Internship Scheme

Best performing startups supported under various schemes

Best performing Youth trained under PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana

Best performing startups supported under Startup India Seed Fund

Best performing MY Bharat Volunteers

Beneficiaries under NAMASTE, PM AJAY, SEED

Students of Delhi government schools, selected from various quizzes, competitions

Saluting the contribution of entrepreneurs, innovators and grass root workers towards Viksit Bharat@2047, special guests have been invited from the following categories:

International Yoga Day Volunteers

Women Entrepreneurs under PM Mudra Yojana

Best performing beneficiaries of PMAY(U)

Innovators/Scientists in different fields

Sarthi/Cab Driver/Taxi Drivers of Bharat Taxi in Delhi

PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana beneficiaries

Artisans under PM Vishwakarma scheme

Best performing beneficiaries under Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) Yojana

Best performing farmers under Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY)

The Special Guests also include the silent warriors, who work hard round-the-clock to assist others in achieving their goals. As Independence Day is a celebration to recognise their contributions as well, special guests from the following categories have been also invited:

Street vendors under PM SVANidhi

Urban sanitation workers under Swachh Bharat Mission

Best performing Delhi Metro workers

Best performing workers of Kartavya Path/Central Vista workers

Nursing Orderlies (Ward Attendants) and other staffs of Government Hospitals in Delhi

Over 1,500 Delhi-based people from various States/Union Territories dressed in traditional attire have also been invited to witness the grand ceremony. They will demonstrate a microcosm of India at Red Fort.

Involving Children through Competitions

In the run up to Independence Day, quizzes and competitions were conducted by Ministry of Defence in collaboration with My Gov. These include Essay Competition on ‘Role of AI in building a Viksit Bharat by 2047’; Painting Competition on ‘India 1947 vs India 2047’; and a series of online quiz contests namely Constitution of India – Fundamental rights, duties, key articles and makers, Women in India’s Freedom Movement – From Rani Lakshmibai to Sarojini Naidu and beyond, Major milestones of Modern India : Technological progresses and achievement in Space Technology, and India’s success story in Nuclear Technology. Around 600 winners of the competitions will also be part of the celebrations.

Other Ministries/Departments, Govt of NCT of Delhi and Delhi Police are also organising various online and offline quizzes and activities to engage citizens in the celebration of this national festival.

Public Convenience

Provision of cloak room: Availability of cloak rooms was applauded by visitors during previous Republic Day and Independence Day Celebrations. For the ease of the people, 25 cloak rooms at six locations have been installed for the forthcoming celebrations.

Volunteers at helpdesk: 200 volunteers - 100 from MY Bharat & 100 from NCC - will assist visitors along with the police personnel in reaching the enclosures. The volunteers can be identified on the way to Red Fort.

Provision of Wheelchair: NCC cadets will be present at metro station and parking areas for all the visitors who need assistance of 20 wheelchairs.

Metro Services: Metro will be operational from 4 AM on 15th August for people to reach the venue. Metro Services will be provided free of cost to all invitees. Metro QR codes will be provided with e-invitation.

Parking facility at Parade Ground: Parking facility will be available for visitors with valid parking/labels.

Ramp facility for pedestrians: To facilitate smooth movement of pedestrians from upper Subhash Marg to lower Subhash Marg, robust ramps and stairs have been installed.

Use of Google & Mappls Maps: On the day of the main event, traffic restrictions will be visible on Google & Mappls Maps for the people.

Rain Ponchos: Owing to the unpredictable weather conditions, rain ponchos will be provided to all invitees in Madhav Das Park and August 15 Park in addition to the dignitaries at the rampart.

Invitation Card: Public Service & Commitment to Duty

The Prime Minister, while dedicating ‘Seva Teerth’ to the nation, said that ‘Seva Teerth’ stands as a radiant and powerful symbol of duty, compassion and commitment to the principle of Nation First. It will inspire generations to walk the path of selfless service and tireless dedication to the welfare of all. With this spirit, the invitation cards for the main event this year showcase ‘Seva Teerth’ to motivate the people to move forward with dedication for the well-being of every citizen. Dharm Chakra on the invitation card symbolises the eternal movement of righteous duty and continuous selfless action.

Swachhta Campaign

With the sense of commitment to duty, this year’s post-event Swachhta Campaign is being organised at Red Fort involving NCC cadets and MY Bharat Volunteers. The objective of the campaign is to ensure systematic plogging and prompt removal of garbage after the dispersal of spectators on the same day and send a message of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan. The campaign will ensure that Red Fort is available after the function for visitors coming from all over the country.

Names of Enclosures

To end VIP culture and underscore the importance of water conservation, the seating enclosures were named after rivers in Republic Day 2026. For the Independence Day Celebrations, the names of the seating enclosures have been named after major lakes of India.

Drainage Management

In view of potential rainfall during the Independence Day Ceremony, several measures have been taken to prevent water overflow. Consequently, drainage and sewage systems in and around the Red Fort and nearby premises are being thoroughly cleaned.

Government of India notifies 11 more International Ports, enabling entry of E-Visa holder foreigners into India

headline: FRAMEWORK FOR BALANCING ELECTRICITY FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY AND AFFORDABILITY
fullText:
Ministry of Power

FRAMEWORK FOR BALANCING ELECTRICITY FINANCIAL SUSTAINABILITY AND AFFORDABILITY

10 AUG 2026 5:42PM by PIB Delhi

Government has established a comprehensive policy and regulatory framework under the provisions of the Electricity Act, 2003 to ensure financial sustainability of the electricity sector while safeguarding consumer interests. The framework comprises, inter alia, the National Electricity Policy, the Tariff Policy, and subordinate legislation framed by the Appropriate Government, Central Electricity Authority, and the Electricity Regulatory Commissions.

Electricity tariffs in India are determined by the Appropriate Electricity Regulatory Commissions under the Electricity Act, 2003. These Commissions are guided by the National Tariff Policy formulated by the Central Government. State Electricity Regulatory Commissions determine the retail tariff considering power procurement, transmission, wheeling and supply costs. State Governments may provide subsidy to any class of consumers including domestic consumers in the tariff determined by the State Commission.

Central Government has taken various initiatives aimed at reducing the cost of electricity. Guidelines have been issued for competitive procurement of electricity by Distribution licensees. Distribution licensees have been enabled to purchase electricity from power exchanges at competitive prices. Under the scheme for flexibility in utilisation of domestic coal, plants supplying electricity to Distribution licensees have been allowed to use cheaper coal for generation. Lower-cost inter-state generating stations are being prioritised for dispatch of electricity. Distribution licensees have also been incentivised to reduce their technical and commercial losses under Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS).

Draft National Electricity Policy, 2026 proposes that distribution licensees prepare Resource Adequacy Plans to ensure least-system-cost based power procurement. It further provides that tariffs should progressively recover fixed costs through demand/fixed charges so that tariff design better reflects the cost of supply while promoting efficient consumption. The Draft Policy also proposes that variations in power purchase costs, including fuel costs, be passed through to consumers through automatic monthly Fuel and Power Purchase Cost Adjustment (FPPCA) mechanisms. Further, it envisages the creation of suitable stabilisation fund to moderate the impact of fluctuations in power purchase costs on consumers.

The Draft Policy further provides that State Electricity Regulatory Commissions should ensure that tariffs progressively reflect the prudent cost of supply without the creation of regulatory assets. It also proposes timely annual tariff revisions, including through suitable indexation-based mechanisms where appropriate, in cases where tariff orders are not issued within the defined timelines, so as to maintain the financial sustainability of distribution licensees.

Consumer protection has been strengthened through the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020, which prescribe standards relating to new electricity connections, quality and reliability of supply, metering, billing, grievance redressal, compensation for specified service deficiencies, and consumer-centric service delivery. In addition, the Draft National Electricity Policy, 2026 proposes that distribution licensees ensure reliable, affordable and quality 24×7 electricity supply, and strengthen grievance redressal through robust online complaint registration, tracking and disposal mechanisms, including virtual hearings by Consumer Grievance Redressal Forums and the Ombudsman.

Government of India has supplemented the efforts of the States earlier through schemes like Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY), Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS), Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA) and currently under Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), to help them achieve the objective of providing quality and reliable supply of power.

In addition to above, to support the power distribution licensees, some of the key initiatives taken, in addition to RDSS, are as under:

Additional Borrowing consent of 0.5% of Gross Sate Domestic Product (GSDP) to State Governments, which is conditional on them undertaking specific reforms in the power sector.

Additional Prudential Norms for sanctioning of loans to State owned power utilities contingent on the performance of power distribution licensees against prescribed conditions.

Rules for implementation of Fuel and Power Purchase Cost Adjustment (FPPCA) and cost reflective tariff so as to ensure that all prudent cost of supply of electricity is passed through.

Rules and Standard Operating Procedure issued for proper subsidy accounting and their timely payment.

(iii) The measures taken by the Government to expand the integration of renewable energy are enclosed at Annexure.

(iv) The Draft National Electricity Policy, 2026 further provides a long-term roadmap for strengthening the power sector by achieving single-digit AT&C losses through smart metering, regular energy audits, GIS-based asset mapping, and consumer indexing. It also proposes strengthening of corporate governance of distribution licensees, introduction of shared distribution networks, and establishment of Distribution System Operators (DSOs) to facilitate integration of distributed renewable energy, energy storage systems and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technologies. For effective transmission capacity expansion and integrating higher shares of renewable energy, the draft policy envisages modernization of the transmission network through adoption of technologies such as Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS), Dynamic Line Rating, underground cabling where appropriate, simplified utilisation-based transmission connectivity, use of dated thermal generating stations as synchronous condensers and accelerated deployment of energy storage systems to support a resilient and flexible grid.

Any impact of changes in fuel prices or electricity demand on consumer tariffs is assessed by the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions in accordance with the applicable tariff regulations, including the Fuel and Power Purchase Cost Adjustment (FPPCA) mechanism, and is allowed to be recovered through tariffs only with due regulatory scrutiny.

Government of India has taken following measures to ensure affordable, reliable and sustainable electricity supply:

As per National Electricity Plan (Generation), installed generation capacity in 2031-32 is likely to be 874 GW. With a view to ensure generation capacity remains ahead of projected demand, all the States, in consultation with CEA, have prepared their “Resource Adequacy Plans (RAPs)”, which are dynamic 10-year rolling plans and includes power generation as well as power procurement planning.

All the States were advised to initiate process for creating/ contracting generation capacities; from all generation sources, as per their Resource Adequacy Plans.

In order to augment the power generation capacity, the Government of India has initiated following capacity addition programme:

a. Thermal Capacity Addition: The projected thermal (coal and lignite) capacity requirement by the year 2035–36 is estimated at approximately 3,15,000 MW. To meet this requirement, Ministry of Power has envisaged to set up an additional minimum 1,05,000 MW coal and lignite based thermal capacity.

Accordingly, Thermal capacities of around 21,080 MW have been commissioned since April 2023 till 30.06.2026. In addition, 47,545 MW of thermal capacity (including 4,845 MW of stressed thermal power projects) is currently under construction. The contracts of 16,000 MW have been awarded and are due for construction.

b. Central Electricity Authority has projected hydro power capacity addition of about 16,448 MW during the period 2026–27 to 2031–32. Of this, 400 MW has been commissioned as on 30.06.2026 and 12,973 MW are presently under construction.

c. Nuclear Capacity Addition: 8,000 MW of nuclear capacity is under construction and targeted to be completed by 2031-32. 5,600 MW of nuclear capacity is under various stages of planning and approval.

d. Renewables Capacity Addition: 1,47,720 MW renewable capacity including 119,580 MW of solar (including Hybrid-Solar) and 27,720 MW of wind (including Hybrid-wind) is under construction while 47,830 MW of renewable capacity including 44,440 MW of solar is at various stages of planning and targeted to be completed by 2029-30.

Addition of Energy Storage Systems: As on 30.06.2026, 15,870 MW/95,220 MWh Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs) are under construction. Further, a total of 6,580 MW/39,480 MWh capacity of PSPs are concurred and yet to be taken up for construction. As on 30.06.2026, 15,754 MW / 42,530 MWh Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity are under construction, 11,747 MW / 38,425 MWh has been awarded and 19,192 MW / 67,574 MWh BESS capacity are under tendering stage.

(iv) Coordinated transmission planning is undertaken in the National Electricity Plan (Transmission) to avoid congestion, minimize curtailment and optimise network augmentation requirements. To address the intermittency associated with RE sources, the Government is promoting a combination of energy storage and hybrid solutions to ensure grid stability and reliable power supply. Under the plan, around 47 GW of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) has been considered for integration by 2031-32. Further, roadmap for integrating 100 GW Pumped Storage Plants (PSPs) from the year 2025-26 to 2035-36 has been prepared.

In addition to the above, the Ministry of Power has issued guidelines dated 14.06.2024, 21.03.2025 and 15.12.2025 regarding the payment of compensation for Right of Way (RoW) for transmission lines, wherein the land rate has been linked to the prevailing market rate. These guidelines address the key challenges of RoW arising from landowners demanding higher compensation than the rates determined by the State Government.

Government of India launched RDSS in July 2021 with the objective of improving the quality and reliability of power supply to consumers through a financially sustainable and operationally efficient distribution Sector. The scheme has an outlay of Rs. 3,03,758 Cr. and estimated Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) from Central Government of Rs. 97,631 Cr. Under the scheme, financial assistance is being provided to the Distribution licensees (excluding Private Sector licensees) for loss reduction infrastructure works and smart metering works. Projects worth Rs. 1.53 lakh crore for loss reduction infrastructure and Rs. 1.31 lakh crore for smart metering works have been sanctioned under the scheme which would help improve the reliability and quality of power supply in the country.

With the concerted effort of Central and State Government, the average hours of supply in rural areas have increased from 12.5 hours in FY14 to 22.6 hours in FY26 and in urban areas the same has increased from 22.1 hours in FY 14 to 23.4 hours in FY26.

A few of the key measures taken by the Government to expand the integration of renewable energy are:

Development of RE Zones and pooling stations, enabling optimal evacuation of large renewable capacities through shared infrastructure;

Setting up of Regional Energy Management Centers (REMCs) for better forecasting of renewable power and to assist grid operators to manage variability and intermittency of renewable power.

Central Government through Ministry of New &Renewable Energy (MNRE) extended budgetary support for the Intra-State transmission projects under Green Energy Corridor (GEC) scheme for integration of RE;

Strengthening of grid operations, including improved forecasting, scheduling, real-time dispatch and ancillary services, to reduce balancing costs;

Market reforms, such as real-time electricity markets and flexibility mechanisms, allowing better utilization of existing resources and lower system integration costs;

As per the Third Amendment to the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission General Network Access (GNA) Regulations, 2022, connectivity is granted separately for solar and non-solar hours by assessing available margins at RE pooling stations, ensuring better utilisation of existing transmission assets and lowering overall system costs;

Connectivity quantum is assessed for hybrid projects to optimise the overall RE quantum, thereby, facilitating efficient grid utilization;

The intra-state transmission network is being strengthened in line with the planned addition of renewable energy capacity. Further, the Inter-State Transmission System (ISTS) for renewable energy schemes are being interconnected with the intra-state transmission network to enhance the overall grid reliability;

A number of state-of-the art Static Synchronous Compensators (STATCOM) and Static VAR Compensator (SVC) are being deployed to dynamically adjust the reactive power flow in the grid for maintaining stable voltage levels;

The generators with high ramp rate (e.g., hydro or gas) are also scheduled optimally to maintain load generation balance.

The Ministry of Heavy Industries has launched the PLI scheme namely “National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage,” approved in May 2021 with a total outlay of ₹18,100 crore to establish 50 GWh of domestic Advanced Chemistry Cell manufacturing capacity, out of which 10 GWh is earmarked for Grid Scale Stationary Storage (GSSS) applications.

MoP in March, 2022 notified the Guidelines for Procurement and Utilization of Battery Energy Storage Systems as part of Generation, Transmission and Distribution assets, along with Ancillary Services.

Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) Guidelines for procurement of ESS (BESS & PSP) by distribution licensees are notified, creating a transparent mechanism for large-scale storage procurement.

A National Framework for Promotion of Energy Storage Systems was issued in September 2023, providing a comprehensive roadmap for deployment, market integration and regulatory facilitation of storage technologies.

Government of India, in September 2023, approved a Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme for development of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). BESS capacity of 13.22 GWh is under implementation with a budgetary allocation of Rs 3,760 Cr. under this scheme. Considering the increasing demand of BESS, Ministry of Power, in June 2025, has approved another VGF scheme for development of 30 GWh BESS capacity with a financial support of Rs 5,400 Cr from Power System Development Fund (PSDF).

100% waiver of ISTS charges for BESS projects commissioned by June 2025 and for Hydro Pumped Storage Projects (PSP) projects wherein construction work is awarded by June, 2025, with 25% annual reduction in waiver thereafter. For Co-located Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) projects, 100% ISTS charges waiver has been extended for the projects commissioned upto June 2028. For PSP projects, 100% ISTS charges waiver has been extended for the projects for which construction work is awarded by June 2028.

MoP, vide order dated 01.08.2025, has increased the limit for concurrence of hydro generating stations, off- stream open loop and on-stream PSP by Central Electricity Authority from ₹1,000 crore to ₹3,000 crore. Further, off-stream closed loop PSPs has been exempted from the requirement of concurrence from the Authority.

In February 2025, CEA issued an advisory on co-location of ESS with solar power projects, recommending storage capacity of at least 10% of installed solar capacity for a minimum duration of two hours, to improve dispatchability of solar power.

Through amendment of the Electricity Rules in September 2025, energy storage systems have been permitted to be developed, owned, leased or operated by consumers, expanding the range of ownership and business models.

This information was given by The Minister of State in the Ministry of Power, Shri Shripad Naik, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

- **Consumer Protection**: Strengthened under the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020, addressing supply quality, billing, reliability, and grievance redressal. Draft policy proposes robust online complaint systems and virtual hearings for consumer forums.  
- **Government Schemes**: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY), Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS), Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (SAUBHAGYA), and ongoing RDSS.  
- **Financial Measures**:  
  - Additional borrowing consent up to 0.5% of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) for state governments, conditional on power sector reforms.  
  - Prudential norms for loans to state-owned utilities tied to distribution licensee performance.  
  - Rules for FPPCA implementation and subsidy accounting.  
- **Renewable Energy Integration**:  
  - Targets 874 GW installed generation capacity by 2031-32 (National Electricity Plan).  
  - Thermal capacity addition of ~105,000 MW by 2035-36 to meet estimated 315,000 MW requirement.  
- **Technical Modernization**:  
  - Goals to reduce AT&C losses via smart metering, GIS-based asset mapping, and regular energy audits.  
  - Introduction of Distribution System Operators (DSOs), shared distribution networks, and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) integration.  
  - Transmission upgrades using Flexible AC Transmission Systems (FACTS), Dynamic Line Rating, and energy storage systems.  
- **Capacity Expansion**: All states are developing Resource Adequacy Plans (RAPs) as dynamic 10-year rolling procurement plans.

Ministry of Power

DISCOMS DIGITALISATION

10 AUG 2026 5:40PM by PIB Delhi

Electricity being a concurrent subject, distribution of electricity to consumers, including the operations of the Distribution Companies (DISCOMs) and digitalisation thereof, falls within the purview of the respective distribution utility, which functions under the guidance of the respective State Government and State Electricity Regulatory Commission. Government of India has supplemented the efforts of the States earlier through various schemes like Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS), launched in December, 2014, National Smart Grid Mission (NSGM), established in 2015, and presently under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), launched in July, 2021 with the objective of improving the quality of power supply through a financially sustainable and operationally efficient distribution sector.

Under IPDS, works amounting to Rs. 58,686 crore were executed, which supported IT enablement of the distribution sector under the subsumed Restructured Accelerated Power Development and Reforms Programme (R-APDRP), which included works for Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), SCADA/ DMS in 59 towns, Real Time-Data Acquisition System (RT-DAS) in 1,414 towns and installation of 6.54 lakh smart meters. The scheme stands closed in March 2022.

The objective of NSGM is to plan and monitor the implementation of policies and programmes related to smart grids in India. The key components of the Mission were assistance in formulation of projects including pre-feasibility studies, project appraisal, funding to projects, and training and capacity building. Under NSGM, 1,45,343 smart meters were installed in the State of Rajasthan and 24,214 smart meters in Chandigarh. A total of Rs 72.27 Cr was released under the Mission, out of which Rs 31.85 Cr was released since FY2023. The Mission stands closed in March 2024.

Under RDSS, financial assistance is being provided to the Distribution Utilities for loss reduction infrastructure works and smart metering works. Projects worth Rs. 1.53 lakh crore for loss reduction infrastructure works and Rs. 1.31 lakh crore for smart metering works have been sanctioned under the scheme. This includes works related to digitalisation of the distribution utilities which, inter alia, include the following:

Smart metering works covering 19.79 crore consumers, 2.05 lakh feeders and 52.53 lakh Distribution Transformers (DTs) and the related digital eco-system.

SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition)/ DMS (Distribution Management System) works sanctioned for 394 towns amounting to Rs. 2,627 crore.

IT/OT works such as Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems, unified billing solutions, GIS-based works and real time data acquisition systems (RT-DAS) amounting to Rs 3,999 Cr.

Smart distribution works amounting to Rs. 8,608 crore sanctioned for seven cities, which include SCADA and smart technology works, GIS substations, Distribution Transformer health management, undergrounding of HT/LT lines and system augmentation/ modernisation works.

Further , to enable the adoption of digitalisation across the country, the Government of India has initiated India Energy Stack (IES), which is envisioned to create a universal digital enablement for data exchange across the power sector.

New-Age Skills Under PMKVY
